# Korean Economic News Broadcast

Good morning. Here is today's Korean economic news briefing.

We begin with urgent developments in the government's all-out effort to stabilize consumer prices. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Goo Yoon-chul announced this afternoon that the third round of oil price controls will take effect from midnight tonight. This decision reflects a comprehensive consideration of rising international crude prices and the need to ease the financial burden on ordinary citizens. The government is implementing this measure as part of a comprehensive task force focused on special management of livelihood prices, with announcements expected at seven o'clock this evening detailing all containment strategies.

The backdrop to these emergency measures is significant inflationary pressure stemming from the Middle East conflict. According to government analysis, without the existing oil price ceiling system, March inflation would have risen by 2.8 percent. To combat this mounting pressure, the government is pursuing a multi-pronged approach extending far beyond energy alone. Price controls on essential goods are being strengthened, with government oversight of all crisis-prone items. Telecommunications costs will be reduced through expanded data peace options and revised age-based rate structures, potentially saving consumers 380 billion won. Government computers will be distributed free of charge to vulnerable populations to reduce their purchasing burden. The government is also strengthening supervision of private academy tuition fees and has announced plans to release government stockpiles of pollock beginning the thirteenth, with supplies continuing through June thirtieth. Mackerel import sources are being diversified, chicken will receive subsidies up to forty percent discount, and additional garlic from government reserves—eighteen hundred tons—will be released to the market.

Turning to fiscal conditions, the overall government budget situation reveals mounting challenges. According to the Planning and Budget Ministry's April fiscal trends report released today, the national budget posted a fourteen trillion won deficit for the first two months of the year. While this represents an improvement of approximately four trillion won compared to the same period last year thanks to increased tax revenues, national debt has ballooned by over forty-four trillion won in just two months. Total government revenue for January and February reached 121 trillion six hundred billion won, up eighteen trillion six hundred billion won year-on-year. National tax revenues increased by ten trillion won to seventy-one trillion won. Income taxes, including wages and capital gains, rose by two trillion four hundred billion won, while value-added tax increased four trillion one hundred billion won. The stock market boom this year generated an additional one trillion two hundred billion won in securities transaction taxes. However, total government expenditure reached one hundred twenty-eight trillion seven hundred billion won, creating a consolidated fiscal deficit of seven trillion one hundred billion won. More alarmingly, national debt stands at one trillion three hundred four trillion five hundred billion won based on last year's figures, having increased by one hundred twenty-nine trillion four hundred billion won in just twelve months. The national debt-to-GDP ratio has already reached forty-nine percent, and when first supplementary budget allocations are included, exceeding fifty percent is anticipated—another record high.

This fiscal deterioration occurs against a backdrop of global economic uncertainty. The Middle East conflict has created significant volatility in international financial markets, though this tension appears to be moderating somewhat following news of a ceasefire. Foreign exchange and financial markets have shown signs of stabilizing. However, the government is maintaining vigilance and pledging total commitment to macroeconomic stability and alleviating livelihood burdens.

In securities markets, Korean stocks showed weakness today. The KOSPI index opened lower, falling 0.66 percent or approximately 39 points to settle around 5,833. Meanwhile, the KOSDAQ performed relatively better, showing recovery. Foreign investors continued net selling, offloading 249 billion seven hundred forty million won in securities. Individual investors and institutional investors provided support, purchasing 20 billion 429 million won and 209 billion 9 hundred million won respectively. By sector, communications stocks advanced 4.87 percent and chemicals rose 1.99 percent, while insurance declined 2.17 percent and construction fell 1.29 percent.

The weakness in Korean equities reflects broader international market pressures. March saw massive foreign capital outflows of 36 billion five hundred million dollars from Korean markets—a stark reversal that has pressured the Korean won. Global stock markets have declined on concerns regarding slowing economic indicators and questions about artificial intelligence investment profitability. Major government bond yields worldwide have risen due to inflation worries stemming from elevated oil prices and diminished expectations for interest rate cuts.

Regarding the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy outlook, minutes from the March Federal Open Market Committee meeting revealed that Fed officials are largely aligned on maintaining interest rate stability for the near term. However, some participants discussed the possibility of rate increases if energy prices driven by conflict escalate inflation. Conversely, others maintained that future rate cuts remain possible if economic weakness materializes. This two-way scenario reflects genuine uncertainty pervading global monetary policy.

In real estate markets, Seoul apartment prices showed signs of deceleration this week. The weekly apartment price appreciation rate for the Seoul metropolitan area as of April sixth was 0.10 percent, down from 0.12 percent the previous week. This marks a slowdown from the accelerating appreciation trend observed since mid-March. Regional variations persist, with outer districts maintaining upward momentum while Gangnam areas continue declining. The Gangnam three districts—Gangnam, Seocho, and Songpa—specifically sustained price decreases. Jeonse lease prices show divergent trends, with most areas appreciating due to supply shortages, though Gangnam experienced a shift to declining prices.

Notable developments include unprecedented competitiveness for premium apartment subscriptions. The Acro de Seocho reconstruction project in Seoul's Seocho district recorded a competition rate of 1,099 to one, the highest ever recorded. The project produced this year's first perfect-score subscription lottery winning ticket, requiring applicants to be seven-member families with over fifteen years of both subscription account tenure and non-property-ownership status.

In industrial news, battery manufacturers face intensifying global competition. According to market research firm SNE Research, Korea's three major battery companies—Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution, and SK Innovation—saw their global market share outside China fall to the thirty-percent range. This represents a significant decline from previous dominance as Chinese competitors capture increasing shares and electric vehicle manufacturers aggressively demand price reductions. Korean battery companies must differentiate through technological advancement and cost management to maintain competitiveness.

LG's AI Research Institute announced development of Exaone 4.5, a multimodal artificial intelligence model capable of simultaneously understanding and reasoning about both text and images. This system excels at analyzing complex real-world documents including contracts, technical drawings, and financial statements commonly used in industrial applications. The model represents advancement toward more sophisticated AI capable of processing diverse data types.

In contrasting international developments, Chinese tech giant Alibaba is investing heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Partnering with state-owned China Telecom, Alibaba is constructing a major AI data center in Guangdong province, deploying approximately ten thousand units of its self-developed Zhenwu semiconductors. These chips simultaneously support AI training and inference, enabling operation of large-scale models with hundreds of billions of parameters. The data center is designed for expansion to eventually accommodate up to one hundred thousand chips and serve applications spanning healthcare and advanced materials sectors.

The Middle East ceasefire announced yesterday temporarily stabilized commodity and currency markets. International crude prices declined approximately fifteen percent following the truce announcement, temporarily easing Korean oil price pressures. The ceasefire, scheduled for two-week duration with potential U.S.-Iran negotiations beginning April eleventh in Pakistan, has reduced immediate geopolitical risk premiums. However, considerable uncertainty remains regarding whether diplomatic efforts will achieve lasting resolution.

For Korean investors and the general public, several implications warrant attention. First, consumer price pressures appear likely to moderate somewhat if the oil market stabilizes, though government interventions will remain necessary. Second, persistent foreign capital outflows and won weakness require careful monitoring of currency risks for those holding overseas assets. Third, employment dynamics warrant close attention given youth unemployment reaching 7.7 percent—double the overall 3.4 percent rate. Fourth, real estate investors should recognize that price dynamics vary significantly by region, with outer areas showing resilience while premium neighborhoods face headwinds. Finally, the technology sector offers potential opportunities as Korean companies advance AI capabilities, though battery industry competition remains intensely challenging.

The government remains committed to stabilizing macroeconomic conditions while supporting vulnerable populations during this period of global uncertainty. Additional details regarding tonight's comprehensive price stability measures will provide further guidance for economic planning and consumer expectations.

This has been today's Korean economic news briefing. Thank you for your attention.
